name: Aloe vera (sinkle bible)
what_people_do: Cut a leaf and use the gel on burns, skin and scalp, or drink it for "sugar"; in rural Somalia aloe gel is also put in the eye.
why_they_say_it_works: The gel is cooling and healing; the bitter drink is believed to treat diabetes.

documented_by.source: Mahabir D, Gulliford MC 1997, Rev Panam Salud Publica, PMID 9128111
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Aloes were among the plants preferentially used for diabetes by Trinidad patients (622 surveyed).

documented_by.source: Traditional Eye Medicine in Rural Somalia, 2026, Clin Ophthalmol, PMID 41907805 (commentary)
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Commentary: aloe liquid or gel is a commonly reported eye remedy in rural Somalia, alongside breast milk, honey and plant sap.

evidence.finding: NCCIH: clinical research suggests aloe gel may speed burn healing and ease burn pain; two small acne studies; not enough reliable information for eczema.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Putting aloe, or any plant material, in the eye risks infection and corneal damage (Somalia commentary); oral aloe latex is a laxative.
gaps: Oral aloe for diabetes untested in my reading.
